title: CHAPTER 2: UNDERSTANDING FOREIGN POLICY AND DIPLOMACY
content: ✨ 👋 እንኳን ወደ የትምህርቱ ቀጣይ ክፍል በሰላም መጣችሁ! በዚህ ክፍል የሀገራት የውጭ ፖሊሲ ባህሪያት (Patterns & Trends)፣ የውጭ ፖሊሲ አቅጣጫዎችና ልኬቶች (Dimensions: Alignment, Scope, and Modus Operandi)፣ እንዲሁም ዋና ዋና የውጭ ፖሊሲ ማስፈጸሚያ መሳሪያዎችን (Diplomacy, Economic Instruments, and Foreign Aid) በዝርዝር እናያለን አብሮነታችሁ አይለየን👇👇። ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📌 2.2.3. Foreign Policy Behavior: Patterns and Trends 🔹 What is Foreign Policy Behavior? - Refers to the concrete actions states take towards each other. - These actions are not ends in themselves, but are tied to larger purposes — ranging from long-range visions to short-term immediate objectives. - Key Reality: The nature of foreign policy involves double standards and inconsistencies. It is misleading to simply categorize states as purely "peace-loving" or "war-like". - 👉 የውጭ ፖሊሲ ባህሪ ማለት ሀገራት እርስ በርሳቸው የሚያደርጓቸው ተግባራዊ እርምጃዎች ናቸው። እነዚህ እርምጃዎች በራሳቸው የመጨረሻ ግብ ሳይሆኑ ትልልቅ የሀገር ግቦችን ለማሳካት የሚያገለግሉ ናቸው። በሁሉም ሀገራት የውጭ ፖሊሲ ውስጥ ድርብ መመዘኛዎች (Double standards) እና አለመጣጣሞች ይስተዋላሉ። 🔹 Arnold Wolfers' Three Patterns of Foreign Policy Behavior Arnold Wolfers, a prominent IR scholar, suggested that all foreign policy behavior ultimately boils down to three patterns: 1. Self-Preservation (Maintaining the Status Quo): - Concept: Seeking to maintain the existing international system and balance of power because it favors the state's interest. - Example: United States (USA): Post-WWII, the US emerged as a global superpower and shaped global institutions (IMF, World Bank, GATT/WTO, UN Security Council with Veto power). - Because the liberal economic-political order serves its interests, the US acts as the primary defender of the status quo and strongly resists or sanctions any attempts to disrupt it. - 👉 Self-preservation (ነባሩን ስርዓት ማስጠበቅ)፦ አሁን ያለው ዓለም አቀፍ ስርዓት የሚጠቅማቸው ሀገራት (ለምሳሌ አሜሪካ) ስርዓቱ እንዳይቀየርና ጥቅማቸው እንዳይነካ የሚከተሉት ባህሪ ነው። 2. Self-Extension (Revising the Status Quo in One's Own Favor): - Concept: Actively competing to restructure existing international institutions and regimes to create a more enabling environment for their national interests. - Example: Emerging powers like China, India, Brazil, and Germany trying to reform global governance structures. - 👉 Self-extension (ዓለም አቀፍ ስርዓቱን ለራስ ጥቅም ማሻሻል)፦ እንደ ቻይና፣ ህንድ እና ብራዚል ያሉ አዳዲስ በለጸጉ/በመበልጸግ ላይ ያሉ ሀገራት ዓለም አቀፍ ተቋማት የእነሱን ብሄራዊ ጥቅም በሚጠቅም መልኩ እንዲቀየሩ የሚያደርጉት ትግል ነው። 3. Self-Abnegation (Revising the Status Quo in Someone Else's Favor): - Concept: Compromising long-term national interest for temporary, immediate relief or to satisfy foreign powers. - Example: Less Developed Countries (LDCs): Weak states heavily dependent on foreign aid fail to pursue autonomous foreign policies and succumb to external pressures, compromising their national interest. - 👉 Self-abnegation (ብሄራዊ ጥቅም አሳልፎ መስጠት)፦ ደካማና በውጭ እርዳታ ላይ የተመሰረቱ ሀገራት ጊዜያዊ ጥቅምን ለማግኘት ሲሉ የረጅም ጊዜ ብሄራዊ ጥቅማቸውን አሳልፈው ሲሰጡ የሚታይ ባህሪ ነው። አሁንም ከአፍሪካ መሪዎች ራስ ላይ አልዎርድም 💡 Exam Hint: የአርኖልድ ቮልፈርስ (Arnold Wolfers) ሶስቱ ሞዴሎች (Self-preservation, Self-extension, Self-abnegation) እና ምሳሌዎቻቸው (USA, Emerging Powers, LDCs) በፈተና ላይ በደንብ የሚጠየቁ ናቸው ስለዚህ ጠበቅ ጠንቀቅ።! ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📌 2.2.4. Foreign Policy Dimensions Foreign policy behavior is analyzed along three primary dimensions: Alignment, Scope, and Modus Operandi. 🔹 1. Alignment Dimension Focuses on alignment choices made by individual states on whether to ally with power blocs or remain neutral: - Alliances: Formal agreements to provide mutual military assistance. Carrying legal weight, benefits (pooling military strength, base access, deterring enemies), and risks (interference in domestic affairs, being dragged into unwanted conflicts). - Neutrality: A formal stance of non-partisanship in world affairs (keeping a low profile to avoid generating enemies). - Example: Switzerland maintained extreme neutrality, even refusing UN membership until 2002. (Risk: No committed military umbrella during global wars). - Affective Orientation (Informal Alignment / Tilting): Aligning or tilting toward a superpower on key strategic issues without a formal alliance treaty. - Example: Israel is not a formal treaty ally of the US, but consistently sides with US strategic interests. - Nonalignment: Promoted by developing countries during the Cold War through the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), advocating for an independent path rejecting both Western and Eastern military blocs, while promoting South-South cooperation. - 👉 Alignment ማለት ሀገራት ወታደራዊ ህብረት መፍጠር (Alliance)፣ ገለልተኛ መሆን (Neutrality)፣ ወይም ከየትኛውም ጎን አለመሰለፍን (Non-alignment) የሚመርጡበት አቅጣጫ ነው። Neutrality እና non-alignment እንዳያምታቷችሁ አንድ የሚመስሉ ነገር ግን ፈፅሞ የተለያዩ ናቼው። 🔹 2. Scope Dimension Refers to the range and geographic reach of a country's foreign policy interests and activities: - Global Actors: Define national interest in global terms, interacting with countries across every region. Have significant military and diplomatic capacity to influence world events. - Example: USA (and historically ex-USSR). China is rapidly moving into global actor status. - Regional Actors: Interact primarily with neighboring states in their immediate geographic area, except for economic/trade ties with global superpowers. - Examples: South Africa in Africa/SADC, India in South Asia. - Isolationism: Extremely narrow foreign policy scope due to geographical remoteness, historical choices, or internal weakness. - Example: Burma (Myanmar) during the 1960s-1970s. (Note: USA, China, and ex-USSR all had historic periods of isolationism before going global). - 👉 Scope ማለት የአንድ ሀገር የውጭ ፖሊሲ የሚሸፍነው ስፋት ነው (ዓለም አቀፋዊ / Global፣ ቀጠናዊ / Regional፣ ወይም ራስን ማግለል / Isolationism)። 🔹 3. Modus Operandi (Mode of Operation) Dimension Refers to the foreign policy methods and strategy used to address international issues: - Multilateralism: Seeking solutions to problems through diplomatic forums involving multiple states (e.g., UN, AU). Enhances collective bargaining power for developing/weak states and avoids high costs of bilateral embassies. - Examples: LDCs, Germany, and Scandinavian countries heavily prefer multilateralism. - Unilateralism: Relying on independent, unilateral action to settle disputes using power, carrot-and-stick diplomacy, intervention, threats, or force. - Examples: Powerful states with strong military/economic muscles that prefer to dictate outcomes directly. - 👉 Modus Operandi ማለት ሀገራት ችግሮችን ለመፍታት የሚጠቀሙበት መንገድ ሲሆን፣ ብዙ ሀገራትን ባቀፈ መድረክ መፍትሄ መፈለግ (Multilateralism) ወይም በግል አቅም ብቻ እርምጃ መውሰድ (Unilateralism) ናቸው። Multilateralism ብዙ ጊዜ የሚጠቀሙበት በማደግ ላይ ያሉ ሀገሮች ሲሆኑ Unilatearlism የሚጠቀሙበት ያደጉ ሀገሮች ናቼው ምክንያቱም ምንም ቢፈጠር ውሳኔያቼውን አፅንቶ የመቀጠል አቅሙ ስላላቼው💪። ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📌 2.2.5. Instruments of Foreign Policy To achieve their foreign policy goals, states utilize key instruments. The primary tools are Diplomacy, Economic Instruments, and Foreign Aid. 📌 A. DIPLOMACY 🔹 Definition & Nature: - A system of structured communication between actors in international relations to pursue objectives peacefully through private and public dialogue. - Diplomacy vs. Foreign Policy: Foreign policy is the strategy/goal; Diplomacy is the essential tool or action used to execute that policy peacefully. - Historical Shift: Shifted from Old Diplomacy (secret, formal, rigid, purely bilateral between ambassadors) to Modern Diplomacy (multilateral, public diplomacy, summitry/leader-to-leader, and involvement of IGOs like UN/EU and INGOs like Greenpeace). - Governing Treaty: Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961). - 👉 ዲፕሎማሲ ማለት በሀገራት መካከል በሰላማዊ መንገድና በውይይት የውጭ ፖሊሲ ግቦችን ለማሳካት የሚያገለግል የመገናኛና የድርድር መሳሪያ ነው። 🔹 Essence of Diplomacy: Bargaining - Settling differences over priorities through an exchange of proposals for mutually acceptable solutions. - Uses the Carrot and Stick approach: - Stick (Punishment/Threat): Threat = hypothetical negative action; Punishment = real negative action. - Carrot (Promise/Reward): Promise = hypothetical future benefit; Reward = actual benefit/reward provided. 🔹 Rules of Effective Diplomacy: 1. Be realistic: Match goals with actual capability. 2. Be careful about what you say: Weigh words carefully. 3. Seek common ground: Maintain flexibility to reach compromise. 4. Understand the other side: Appreciate opponent's perspective. 5. Be patient: Avoid rush decisions that signal weakness. 6. Leave avenues of retreat open: Allow opponents to "save face" and avoid backing them into a corner. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📌 B. ECONOMIC INSTRUMENTS OF FOREIGN POLICY 🔹 Purposes of Economic Instruments (K.J. Holsti): 1. Exploit dependency to achieve foreign policy goals by offering rewards or threatening economic punishment. 2. Increase a state's own capability or deprive potential enemies of capabilities. 3. Create economic satellites (guaranteed markets and raw material sources). 🔹 Conditions for Effectiveness: - Target state must perceive a genuine need for the reward or avoidance of punishment. - No easy alternative markets or suppliers are available to the target state. 🔹 Key Techniques of Economic Control: - Tariffs: Upward/downward tax manipulation on imports to punish or reward foreign products. - Quotas: Setting strict volume limits on foreign commodities allowed into the country. - Boycott: Government-enforced restriction eliminating the import of goods from a target country. - Embargo: Government prohibition preventing its businessmen from exporting goods (especially strategic materials) to a target country. - Loans, Credits, & Currency Manipulation: Offering favorable terms/loans to friends or manipulating exchange rates to penalize target economies. - 👉 ኢኮኖሚያዊ መሳሪያዎች፡ ታሪፍ (Tariff)፣ ኮታ (Quota- በምርቶች ላይ የመጠን አገዳ መጣል)፣ ቦይኮት (Boycott - ከሌላ ሀገር ዕቃ አለማስገባት) እና ኢምባርጎ (Embargo - ወደ ሌላ ሀገር ዕቃ እንዳይወጣ መከልከል) ናቸው። ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📌 C. FOREIGN AID 🔹 Concept & Types: - Transfer of money, goods, or technical advice from donor to recipient states. - Types: Military Aid, Technical Assistance, Grants/Commodity Import Programs, and Development Loans. 🔹 Military Aid: - The oldest form of aid, used to strengthen alliances and safeguard donor security without deploying donor troops. - Example: US supplying billions in military aid to Saudi Arabia and Iran in the 1960s/70s to preserve regional status quo and secure oil transportation routes. 🔹 Political & Economic Strategic Uses of Aid: - Aid is rarely purely humanitarian; a huge portion goes to strategically/symbolically vital states (e.g., Israel, Egypt, India, Pakistan). - Aid is often "tied" with conditions requiring political/economic reforms (e.g., adopting liberal democracy, market deregulation) or aligning foreign policy with the donor. - 👉 የውጭ እርዳታ (Foreign Aid) በብዛት ለሰብአዊነት ብቻ ሳይሆን የለጋሾችን ፖለቲካዊና ወታደራዊ ፍላጎቶች ለማስፈጸም የሚያገለግል መሳሪያ ነው። ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 👋 የዛሬው ክላሳችን ይሄን ይመስላል፣ በቀጣይ የዚህን ምዕራፍ የመጨረሻ ክፍል 3 (PART 3 ) እንቀጥላለን ። በርቱ፣ መልካም ጥናት ይሁንላችሁ! 🙏🙏🙏
